newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria bulldozes thousands of pirate CDs.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria bulldozes thousands of pirate CDs.

text.p: Bulgarian customs officers on Friday bulldozed a pile of more than 91,000 pirated compact discs worth about $2 million to display their determination to crack down on ilegal production.

"This is only part of all bootleg CDs seized at border checkpoints in the last 18 months. The remainder is in storage as police have not yet completed their investigation," Sofia customs chief Boiko Ivanov told reporters invited to witness the destruction.

The international recording industry is pressing Bulgaria to stop production of high quality pirate CDs which it says are flowing into Russia alone at a rate of one million a month. From there they are distributed to the Baltic states, Finland, Scandinavia and on to the world market.
The International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI) says Bulgaria is second only to China in the export of pirated CDs.
Dimitar Enchev, director of the National Centre for Copyright Protection at the Ministry of Culture said seven production lines were currently operating in Bulgaria.
"The full capacity of the lines is up to 12 million CDs per year while domestic annual consumption is up to 700,000 CDs," Enchev told reporters. "Obviously the remainder is for export."
Bulgaria took its first case to court last month but the defendant was acquitted for lack of evidence.

Police said they had investigated more than 280 producers and vendors of CDs this year in Sofia and in the towns of Botevgrad, Veliko Tarnovo and Stara Zagora, inspecting production lines and stores and confiscating their illegal production.
